   479	cmd_record_round() {
   480	  [[ -n "$gate" && -n "$file" ]] || usage
   481	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: record-round: no feedback file at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
   482	  local p th ts now out trip
   483	  p=$(fb_parse "$file" "$gate")
   484	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.approved' <<<"$p")" == true ]]; then
   485	    echo "recorded: $gate APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged"
   486	    return 0
   487	  fi
   488	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
   489	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
   490	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
   491	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
   492	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
   493	  ts=$(now_iso); now=$(date +%s)
   494	  atomic_update "$breaker" --argjson p "$p" --argjson th "$th" --arg ts "$ts" --argjson now "$now" \
   495	      --arg gate "$gate" --arg sprint "$sprint" "$JQ_DEFS"'
   496	    (if type == "object" and (.triggers | type) == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   497	    | ($p.counts | tojson) as $c
   498	    | (if $p.hash != "none" and $p.hash == (.triggers.same_issue.last_hash // null)
   499	       then .triggers.same_issue.count = ((.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) + 1)
   500	       else .triggers.same_issue.count = 1 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $p.hash end)
   501	    | (if (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts // null) != null and .triggers.no_progress.last_counts == $c
   502	       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
   503	       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
   504	    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c
   505	    | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ((.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) + 1)
   506	    | (.triggers.timeout.started // null | epoch) as $start
   507	    | ( if .triggers.same_issue.count >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
   508	          then ["same_issue", "same issue hash \($p.hash[0:8]) seen \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times in a row"]
   509	        elif .triggers.no_progress.count >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
   510	          then ["no_progress", "finding counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds"]
   511	        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
   512	          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
   513	        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)
   514	          then ["timeout", "run older than \(.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) hours"]
   515	        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
   516	        else null end ) as $trip
   517	    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}
   518	    | if $trip != null and $trip[0] != "open" and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
   519	      then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end)}])
   520	      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"
   521	      else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end
   522	    | .last_trip = $trip' || return 3
   523	  trip=$(jq -r '.last_trip // empty | if type == "array" then "\(.[0]): \(.[1])" else empty end' "$breaker")
   524	  out=$(jq -r '"recorded: \(.last_round.gate) \(.last_round.verdict // "no verdict") — cycle \(.triggers.cycle_count.current)/\(.triggers.cycle_count.limit), same_issue \(.triggers.same_issue.count)/\(.triggers.same_issue.threshold), no_progress \(.triggers.no_progress.count)/\(.triggers.no_progress.threshold)"' "$breaker")
   525	  echo "$out"
   526	  if [[ -n "$trip" ]]; then
   527	    atomic_update "$state_file" --arg ts "$ts" '.state = "HALTED"' || return 3
   528	    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
   529	    return 10
   530	  fi
   531	  return 0
   532	}

   534	cmd_mark() {
   535	  [[ -n "$skill" && -n "$sprint" ]] || usage
   536	  mkdir -p "$run_dir"
   537	  atomic_update "$run_dir/implement-active.json" --arg k "$skill" --arg s "$sprint" --arg ts "$(now_iso)" \
   538	    '{skill: $k, sprint: $s, started_at: $ts}' || return 3
   539	  if [[ -f "$file" ]]; then
   540	    local err drc=0
   541	    err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
   542	    if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
   543	  fi
   544	  echo "marked: $skill $sprint ($run_dir/implement-active.json)"
   545	}
   546	
   547	case "$sub" in
   548	  write)  cmd_write ;;
   549	  read)   cmd_read ;;
   550	  derive) cmd_derive ;;
   551	  record-round) cmd_record_round ;;
   552	  mark)   cmd_mark ;;
   553	  unmark) rm -f -- "$run_dir/implement-active.json" "$run_dir/implement-active.json.lock"; echo "unmarked" ;;
   554	  *) usage ;;
   555	esac

ok 8 KS-8 knob off is silent: no state, no summary, no stderr
ok 9 KS-9 content never reaches state, summary or trajectory
ok 10 KS-10 a symlinked state directory or task file is not written through
not ok 11 KS-11 malformed or foreign payloads are a silent no-op

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# Issue #961 K-1 — Karpathy surgical-diff hook
# =============================================================================
# Pins the contract for .claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:
# fires `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line + trajectory event when the
# session diff accumulator exceeds `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task`,
# while remaining non-blocking (always exits 0) per v1 invariant.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$REPO_ROOT/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    [[ -x "$HOOK" ]] || skip "hook not executable"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"

    TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
    # cycle-129 D-4.3: per-task state under KARPATHY_STATE_DIR; with no run in
    # progress (empty LOA_RUN_DIR) the key is the session id.
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$TMP_DIR/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$TMP_DIR/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$TMP_DIR/legacy-task-state.jsonl"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$TMP_DIR/run"
    export LOA_SESSION_ID="test-session"
    KARPATHY_TASK_STATE="$KARPATHY_STATE_DIR/test-session.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$TMP_DIR/trajectory"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$TMP_DIR/config.yaml"

    # Default test config — surgical_diff_warning on, threshold deliberately
    # tiny so we can trip it with a few small Write calls.
    cat > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE" <<EOF
karpathy_principles:
  surgical_diff_warning: true
  diff_lines_per_task: 5
  enforce: warn
EOF
}

+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. Library mode applies only when the file is sourced. An executed hook ignores the variable.
+- **Remaining gap.** A body written to a plain file by one command and executed by a later command is outside a per-command fence. The Write tool shares this limit.

This is a preserved false positive, never a bypass: leaving `$(`/backtick values un-redacted is what keeps command-substitution smuggling (`git commit -m "$(rm -rf /)"`) caught. # Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?
# Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json, .run/simstim-state.json, .run/state.json
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
_ig_fresh() {
    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
    local now last_epoch
    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
    else
        last_epoch=$(date -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -jf '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
    fi
    [[ "$last_epoch" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    (( last_epoch > 0 && now - last_epoch <= 86400 && last_epoch - now <= 86400 ))
}

# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $2 parses, is at most $1 seconds old and at most 300 s ahead (clock skew);
# jq's fromdateiso8601 keeps it portable (no GNU date -d). Fractional seconds are dropped first
_ig_within() {
    [[ -n "$2" && "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    jq -en --arg t "$2" --argjson w "$1" \
        '($t | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $e | $e != null and (now - $e) <= $w and ($e - now) <= 300' \
        >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# derived_at, when a cache carries one, must be within run_mode.stale_hours (cycle-129 D-4.1)
_ig_derived_ok() {
    local da
    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$1" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
    [[ -z "$da" ]] && return 0
    _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"
}

check_implementation_active() {
    # Check sprint-plan state
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
        local state plan_id last_activity
        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true

        # Integrity: must have plan_id
        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi

        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
        fi

        # A derived cache older than run_mode.stale_hours is not a run position (cycle-129 D-4.1)
        if ! _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json"; then
            return 1
        fi

        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
        local phase simstim_activity
        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
        local run_state run_activity
        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity" && _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/state.json"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    return 1
}

    jq -en --arg t "$2" --argjson w "$1" \
        '($t | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $e | $e != null and (now - $e) <= $w and ($e - now) <= 300' \
        >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# derived_at, when a cache carries one, must be within run_mode.stale_hours (cycle-129 D-4.1)
_ig_derived_ok() {
    local da
    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$1" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
    [[ -z "$da" ]] && return 0
    _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"
}

check_implementation_active() {
    # Check sprint-plan state
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
        local state plan_id last_activity
        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true

        # Integrity: must have plan_id
        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi

        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
        fi

        # A derived cache older than run_mode.stale_hours is not a run position (cycle-129 D-4.1)
        if ! _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json"; then
            return 1
        fi

        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
        local phase simstim_activity
        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
        local run_state run_activity
        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity" && _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/state.json"; then
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    return 1
}

if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  return 0
}

bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  local js st
  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")
  if [[ -z "$s" || -z "$p" ]]; then reason="malformed checkpoint"
  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
  fi
  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
    return 0
  fi
  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  local v
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}
cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# loa-decisions-surface.sh: SessionStart hook that surfaces pending decision rows.
#
# Prints up to 10 `proposed` then `open` rows of grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml (id, status,
# summary only) so the operator sees what awaits /decisions confirm. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on
# `decisions.surface_at_session_start` (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
#
# CONTRACT (observability, never a gate; same as loa-kf-surface.sh):
#   - Exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session.
#   - Disabled or no config: prints nothing (read with yq, or a plain-text fallback without it).
#   - Enabled but Mike Farah yq v4 or jq is missing, or the ledger is unreadable or has an
#     unknown schema_version: one "[DECISIONS] WARNING ..." line on stdout.
#   - Enabled and healthy: the block on stdout (SessionStart injects stdout as context);
#     nothing when no row is open or proposed and no marker is stale.
#   - A stale .run/unattended.json (another session, or older than
#     decisions.unattended_marker_ttl_hours, default 24) adds one notice line.
#
# TRUST BOUNDARY: row text is agent-authored and UNTRUSTED. Only id, status and summary are
#   read; each summary is control-stripped (C0, C1, U+2028/9), angle brackets are replaced so
#   no tag can close the fence, and it is capped at 100 characters. The whole block is then
#   wrapped by the L6 data fence, sanitize_for_session_start L6 <block> --max-chars 2000
#   (context-isolation-lib.sh). Without that sanitizer the block is not printed.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"

# Test seam (mirrors loa-kf-surface.sh): overrides are honoured only under
# LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats marker present.
_dec_test_mode_active() {
  [[ "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" || -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]
}

have_yq4=0
if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1 || true)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]]; then have_yq4=1; fi

# The config is read first (yq, or a plain-text fallback without it), so an enabled surface on a host
# without its tools says so instead of looking disabled.
config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
enabled="false"
if _dec_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
  enabled="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
elif [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
  if [[ $have_yq4 -eq 1 ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
      enabled="$(loa_knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
  else
    # top-level `decisions:` block, then an indented `surface_at_session_start: true`
    enabled="$(awk '
      /^[^[:space:]#]/ { blk = ($0 ~ /^decisions:[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/) }
      blk && /^[[:space:]]+surface_at_session_start:[[:space:]]*true[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/ { print "true"; exit }
    ' "$config_path" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi
fi
[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0

missing=""
[[ $have_yq4 -eq 1 ]] || missing="Mike Farah yq v4"
command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="${missing:+${missing} and }jq"
if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: the decisions surface is enabled but ${missing} is missing; rows are not shown. Install it, or set decisions.surface_at_session_start: false."
  exit 0
fi

LEDGER="${REPO_ROOT}/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
RUN_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/.run"
if _dec_test_mode_active; then
  [[ -n "${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE:-}" ]] && LEDGER="${LOA_DECISIONS_FILE}"
  [[ -n "${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR:-}" ]] && RUN_DIR="${LOA_DEC_SURFACE_RUN_DIR}"
fi

if [[ ! -r "$LEDGER" ]]; then
  echo "[DECISIONS] WARNING: the decision ledger is unreadable at grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml; the surface is enabled but degraded."
  exit 0
fi

# =============================================================================
# loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-098 Sprint 6C).
#
# At session start, identify the current operator (via git config user.email
# → OPERATORS.md slug match), then surface any unread L6 handoffs addressed
# to them. Body content is sanitized via context-isolation-lib's
# sanitize_for_session_start("L6", body) before reaching session context.
#
# This hook is silent (exit 0 with no stdout) when:
#   - structured_handoff.enabled is not true in .loa.config.yaml
#   - operator slug cannot be resolved (no git config user.email match)
#   - no unread handoffs for this operator
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)"
LIB="${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/structured-handoff-lib.sh"
[[ -f "$LIB" ]] || exit 0

# Gate on config.
if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
    enabled="false"
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
        enabled="$(loa_knob structured_handoff.enabled false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
    [[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
else
    # No config → silent (the primitive is opt-in).
    exit 0
fi

# Resolve current operator slug from git config.
git_email="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" config user.email 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
[[ -n "$git_email" ]] || exit 0

# Source operator-identity to map email → slug. Fall back: skip surfacing.

# =============================================================================
# Karpathy Principles (#961 enforcement v1)
# =============================================================================
# Mechanical reinforcement of the 4 Karpathy principles documented inline in
# .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md (post-PR #960) and detailed in
# .claude/protocols/karpathy-principles.md.
#
# v1 ships:
#   - Surgical-Changes diff-size hook (warn-by-default, opt-in BLOCK reserved for v2)
#   - Goal-Driven success-criteria gate in /implement
#   - Trajectory logging at grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/karpathy-*.jsonl
karpathy_principles:
  # Advisory — used by skills' Think-Before-Coding internal checks. No hook
  # consumer in v1; reserved for v2 when surface-assumption analysis lands.
  surface_assumptions: true

  # Simplicity enforcement intensity: full (default, enforced — the YAGNI ladder,
  # stdlib/native first, shortest diff) or ultra (deletion-first, challenges the
  # requirement before building). There is NO advise-only 'lite' level: the
  # "never simplify away" floor (C-PROC-011) stays enforced at every level.
  simplicity_intensity: full

  # G-1 — master switch for the PostToolUse:Write|Edit surgical-diff hook
  # at .claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh. When false,
  # the hook fast-paths to exit 0 in <10ms.
  surgical_diff_warning: true

  # G-1 — per-session diff-lines threshold. When the session accumulator
  # exceeds this, the hook emits a [karpathy-surgical-warn] stderr line
  # and writes a trajectory event. Raised from the original protocol-doc
  # sketch of 50 because 50 was empirically too tight for bug-fix sprints
  # that legitimately touch 60-80 lines (test file + production diff).
  diff_lines_per_task: 100

  # Reserved for v2 — no v1 consumer. Cyclomatic complexity check.
  simplicity_check: true

  # Reserved for v2 — no v1 consumer. AST-level abstraction-depth analysis.
  max_abstraction_depth: 2

  # G-3 — when true, /implement refuses to write code if sprint.md lacks a
  # "Success criteria" / "Acceptance criteria" / "Verification" section.
  # Operator can [Skip with rationale] to override per-invocation.
  require_success_criteria: true

  # warn | block. v1 honors only "warn" — block-mode is reserved for v2 to
  # avoid surprise breaking changes during initial rollout. Even with
  # `enforce: block` set, the v1 hook returns 0 (informational only).
  enforce: warn

# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |

Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh — byte budgets for the always-loaded prompt surface
     4	#
     5	# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1). The prompt surface Claude loads on every turn or on
     6	# every skill invocation has hard byte budgets; this is the CI gate behind them.
     7	#
     8	#   .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md      ≤ 16,384 B  each — charged with every
     9	#                                  resources/*.md the skill reads UNCONDITIONALLY
    10	#   .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      ≤ 9,445 B (cycle-129 D-3.3: min(previous cap, measured 9,189 B + 256 B); the cap never rises)
    11	#   .claude/protocols/*.md (total) ≤ 160,000 B fail; > 114,688 B warns (reference/ is not counted)
    12	#
    13	# Resource charging rule (the byte budget cannot be met by moving text into a
    14	# file the skill still always loads): a resources/<name>.md is charged when a
    15	# SKILL.md line names it AND reads as an unguarded read imperative —
    16	#   imperative: (?i)\b(read|load|source|include)\b          e.g. "Read `resources/X.md`"
    17	#   guard:      (?i)\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b
    18	# A line with a guard word ("See resources/X.md §Security", "read X.md if …") is
    19	# a pointer, not a load, and is not charged. Pinned by tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats.
    20	#
    21	# Every other SKILL.md figure the sprint report needs from the "mechanical pass"
    22	# (history tokens per file) rides along in --json as `history_tokens` —
    23	# informational; enforcement of that rule is tests/unit/no-history-in-rule-text.bats.
    24	#
    25	# Usage:
    26	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh              # human table, exit 1 on any breach
    27	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json       # machine-readable report
    28	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root DIR   # check a fixture tree (tests / CI sentinels)
    29	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --quiet      # exit code only
    30	#
    31	# Exit codes: 0 within budget · 1 breach · 2 usage / missing root
    32	# =============================================================================
    33	set -euo pipefail
    34	export LC_ALL=C
    35	
    36	ROOT="."
    37	JSON=0
    38	QUIET=0
    39	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    40	  case "$1" in
    41	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    42	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    43	    --quiet|-q) QUIET=1; shift ;;
    44	    --help|-h) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    45	    *) echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    46	  esac
    47	done
    48	[[ -d "$ROOT/.claude" ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: no .claude/ under $ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }
    49	
    50	python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$JSON" "$QUIET" <<'PY'
    51	import glob, json, os, re, sys
    52	root, as_json, quiet = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] == "1", sys.argv[3] == "1"
    53	SKILL_LIMIT, LOA_LIMIT, PROTO_FAIL, PROTO_WARN = 16384, 9445, 160000, 114688
    54	IMPERATIVE = re.compile(r"\b(read|load|source|include)\b", re.I)
    55	GUARD = re.compile(r"\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b", re.I)
    56	HISTORY = re.compile(r"cycle-[0-9]{3}|#[0-9]{3,4}|KF-[0-9]{3}")
    57	RES = re.compile(r"resources/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.md)")
    58	
    59	def size(p):
    60	    return os.path.getsize(p)
    61	
    62	violations, skills = [], []
    63	for skill_md in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, ".claude/skills/*/SKILL.md"))):
    64	    sdir = os.path.dirname(skill_md)
    65	    name = os.path.basename(sdir)
    66	    charged, seen = [], set()
    67	    text = open(skill_md, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    68	    for ln, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
    69	        for m in RES.finditer(line):
    70	            rel = m.group(1)
    71	            if rel in seen or not IMPERATIVE.search(line) or GUARD.search(line):
    72	                continue
    73	            rp = os.path.join(sdir, "resources", rel)
    74	            if os.path.isfile(rp):
    75	                seen.add(rel)
    76	                charged.append({"path": os.path.relpath(rp, root), "bytes": size(rp), "line": ln})
    77	    total = size(skill_md) + sum(c["bytes"] for c in charged)
    78	    ok = total <= SKILL_LIMIT
    79	    skills.append({"skill": name, "path": os.path.relpath(skill_md, root), "skill_md_bytes": size(skill_md),
    80	                   "charged_resources": charged, "total": total, "limit": SKILL_LIMIT, "ok": ok,
    81	                   "history_tokens": len(HISTORY.findall(text))})
    82	    if not ok:
    83	        extra = f" (+{len(charged)} charged resource(s))" if charged else ""
    84	        violations.append(f"skill {name}: {total} B > {SKILL_LIMIT} B{extra}")
    85	
    86	loa_path = os.path.join(root, ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md")
    87	loa = {"path": ".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md", "bytes": size(loa_path) if os.path.isfile(loa_path) else 0,
    88	       "limit": LOA_LIMIT, "present": os.path.isfile(loa_path)}
    89	loa["ok"] = loa["bytes"] <= LOA_LIMIT
    90	if not loa["ok"]:
    91	    violations.append(f"CLAUDE.loa.md: {loa['bytes']} B > {LOA_LIMIT} B")
    92	
    93	pfiles = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, ".claude/protocols/*.md")))
    94	protos = [{"path": os.path.relpath(p, root), "bytes": size(p)} for p in pfiles]
    95	ptotal = sum(p["bytes"] for p in protos)
    96	protocols = {"total": ptotal, "count": len(protos), "fail_limit": PROTO_FAIL, "warn_limit": PROTO_WARN,
    97	             "ok": ptotal <= PROTO_FAIL, "warn": PROTO_WARN < ptotal <= PROTO_FAIL, "files": protos}
    98	if not protocols["ok"]:
    99	    violations.append(f"protocols total: {ptotal} B > {PROTO_FAIL} B")
   100	
   101	report = {"ok": not violations, "skills": skills, "claude_loa": loa, "protocols": protocols, "violations": violations}
   102	if as_json:
   103	    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
   104	elif not quiet:
   105	    print(f"{'skill':<32}{'SKILL.md':>10}{'charged':>10}{'total':>10}  limit {SKILL_LIMIT}")
   106	    for s in skills:
   107	        flag = "" if s["ok"] else "  BREACH"
   108	        print(f"{s['skill']:<32}{s['skill_md_bytes']:>10}{sum(c['bytes'] for c in s['charged_resources']):>10}{s['total']:>10}{flag}")
   109	    print(f"CLAUDE.loa.md {loa['bytes']} B (limit {LOA_LIMIT}){'' if loa['ok'] else '  BREACH'}")
   110	    pw = "  WARN (> %d)" % PROTO_WARN if protocols["warn"] else ("" if protocols["ok"] else "  BREACH")
   111	    print(f"protocols total {ptotal} B over {len(protos)} files (fail > {PROTO_FAIL}){pw}")
   112	if violations and not quiet and not as_json:
   113	    print("\nBUDGET BREACH:", file=sys.stderr)
   114	    for v in violations:
   115	        print("  " + v, file=sys.stderr)
   116	elif protocols["warn"] and not quiet and not as_json:
   117	    print(f"WARN: protocols total {ptotal} B exceeds the {PROTO_WARN} B warning threshold", file=sys.stderr)
   118	sys.exit(1 if violations else 0)
   119	PY
     1	name: Prompt Budget
     2	
     3	# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1): the always-loaded prompt surface has hard byte
     4	# budgets — SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read resources),
     5	# CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 9,445 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn > 114,688 B).
     6	# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh is the gate; the two sentinel steps prove the
     7	# gate itself still bites (a scanner that exits 0 from a syntax error must not
     8	# read as green).
     9	
    10	on:
    11	  # Every pull request: the gate takes seconds, and a path filter would miss the
    12	  # shared inputs the checker charges (skill includes rendered into SKILL.md,
    13	  # resources read unconditionally, the keep list) — Bridgebuilder F-001 on
    14	  # PR #1266.
    15	  pull_request:
    16	  push:
    17	    branches: [main]
    18	
    19	jobs:
    20	  prompt-budget:
    21	    name: Byte budgets for the prompt surface
    22	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    23	    timeout-minutes: 5
    24	    steps:
    25	      - name: Checkout
    26	        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
    27	        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
    28	
    29	      - name: Check budgets
    30	        run: |
    31	          set -euo pipefail
    32	          rc=0
    33	          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json > prompt-budget.json || rc=$?
    34	          # A checker that dies before writing a report must fail LOUD with its
    35	          # exit code, not as an opaque jq parse error (Bridgebuilder F-003).
    36	          if ! jq -e . prompt-budget.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    37	            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh --json produced no parseable report (exit $rc)"
    38	            cat prompt-budget.json || true
    39	            exit 1
    40	          fi
    41	          # Human-readable table for the log; the JSON gate below is the verdict.
    42	          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh || echo "::notice::human-readable run exited non-zero; the JSON gate decides"
    43	          jq -r '.violations[]? | "::error::prompt budget: \(.)"' prompt-budget.json
    44	          jq -e '.ok' prompt-budget.json >/dev/null
    45	
    46	      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the over-budget sentinel with exit 1)
    47	        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
    48	        run: |
    49	          set -euo pipefail
    50	          rc=0
    51	          bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over --quiet || rc=$?
    52	          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
    53	            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh did not reject tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/over with exit 1 (got $rc)"
    54	            exit 1
    55	          fi
    56	          echo "OK: over-budget sentinel rejected"
    57	
    58	      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the under-budget sentinel)
    59	        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
    60	        run: |
    61	          set -euo pipefail
    62	          if ! bash tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under --quiet; then
    63	            echo "::error::check-prompt-budget.sh false-positive on tests/fixtures/prompt-budget/under"
    64	            exit 1
    65	          fi
    66	          echo "OK: under-budget sentinel accepted"
    67	
    68	      - name: Upload report
    69	        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real budget failure above stays the visible failure (Bridgebuilder iter-5 F-003)
    70	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
    71	        with:
    72	          name: prompt-budget-report
    73	          path: prompt-budget.json
    74	          retention-days: 14

    if [[ "$cp" == "lightweight" && "$caps" != "null" && "$caps" != "all" ]]; then
        local wf
        wf=$(echo "$frontmatter" | yq eval '.capabilities.write_files' - 2>/dev/null) || wf="null"
        if [[ "$wf" == "true" ]]; then
            log_warning "$skill_name" "cost-profile: lightweight but capabilities.write_files: true (correlation mismatch)" || has_error=true
        fi

    # effort is optional. When present it must be a valid level. A
    # deep-reasoning (xhigh/max) effort paired with a lightweight cost-profile
    # is a suspicious combination (cheap-tier skill asking for the deepest
    # reasoning) → WARN, not ERROR.
    local effort

    if [[ -n "$effort" ]]; then

log "WARNING: Target file not found: $s_target, skipping"
      continue
    fi

    target_sections["$s_target"]+="${s_name} "
    section_data["$s_name"]="${s_target}|${s_template}|${s_filter}"
  done

  if [[ ${#target_sections[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    log "No sections to generate"
    return 0
  fi

  # Phase 1: Create staged copies
  declare -A staged_files
  trap 'for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done' EXIT

  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp
    tmp=$(mktemp "${target}.constraint-XXXXXX")
    cp "$target" "$tmp"
    staged_files["$target"]="$tmp"
  done

  # Phase 2: Render and apply all sections to staged copies
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local tmp="${staged_files[$target]}"
    for section in ${target_sections[$target]}; do
      local s_data="${section_data[$section]}"
      local s_target s_template s_filter
      IFS='|' read -r s_target s_template s_filter <<< "$s_data"

      local o_heading
      if o_heading=$(optional_table_heading "$section"); then
        local o_rows
        o_rows=$(jq -r "$s_filter | length" "$REGISTRY")
        if [[ "$o_rows" == "0" ]]; then
          if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" != "true" ]] && ! prune_optional_table "$tmp" "$section" "$o_heading"; then
            log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
            return 1
          fi
          continue
        fi
      fi

      verbose "Rendering section: $section"
      local content
      content=$(render_section "$section" "$s_template" "$s_filter")

      if [[ "$BOOTSTRAP" == "true" ]]; then
        bootstrap_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"
      else
        if ! insert_generated_section "$tmp" "$section" "$content"; then
          log "ERROR: Generation failed for section '${section}' — no files modified"
          return 1
        fi
      fi
    done
  done

  # Phase 3: Diff or commit
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]] && [[ "$BOOTSTRAP_CONFIRM" != "true" ]]; then
    for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
      log "Diff for ${target}:"
      diff -u "$target" "${staged_files[$target]}" || true
    done
    for tmp in "${staged_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$tmp"; done
    trap - EXIT
    return 0
  fi

  # Commit with rollback
  declare -A backup_files
  for target in "${!target_sections[@]}"; do
    local bak="${target}.constraint-bak"
    cp "$target" "$bak"
    backup_files["$target"]="$bak"
  done

  local commit_failed=false
  local committed=()

+## Rules and arming
+
+These five rules govern every team. Until cycle-129 they were the C-TEAM rows of `constraints.json`, rendered into the always-loaded kernel on every turn; they now live here only (DEC-0140), because no harness surface runs on teammate spawn and the rows cost every single-agent session their bytes. The ids stay as names.
+
+| Id | Rule | Why |
+|----|------|-----|
+| C-TEAM-001 | Planning, orchestration, deployment and lifecycle skills are lead-only; teammates implement, review and audit only (the Skill Invocation Matrix below is the full list) | Planning skills produce single artifacts (PRD, SDD, sprint plan) that assume single-writer semantics; concurrent invocation would corrupt state |
+| C-TEAM-002 | All beads (`br`) operations go through the lead; teammates report via SendMessage | Beads uses SQLite with single-writer semantics; concurrent br sync or br close causes lock contention and potential corruption |
+| C-TEAM-003 | Only the lead writes `.run/` state files (`simstim-state.json`, `bridge-state.json`, `sprint-plan-state.json`); teammates report status via SendMessage | State files use read-modify-write pattern; concurrent writes cause lost updates and inconsistent reads |
+| C-TEAM-004 | Git commit and push go through the lead; teammates report completed work via SendMessage | Git's working tree and index are shared mutable state; concurrent commits or pushes cause merge conflicts, index lock failures, and corrupted state |
+| C-TEAM-005 | Teammates never modify the System Zone (`.claude/`): framework configuration, constraint definitions, hook scripts and schema files are lead-only | System Zone modifications by a teammate could alter constraint definitions, hook behavior, or skill configurations for all agents in the team, breaking the coordination invariants that other C-TEAM constraints depend on |
+
+**Arming.** The three team hooks (`team-role-guard.sh`, `team-role-guard-write.sh`, `team-skill-guard.sh`) stay registered but are no-ops until the lead exports `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` (the teammate's name) into each teammate's environment before spawning it. Without that variable the rules above are prose the teammate is asked to follow, and the review and audit gates are the safety net. The guard register lists the three hooks as `dormant` with `LOA_TEAM_MEMBER` as their knob (`.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml`).

    local name="$1"; shift
    local dis=""
    [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && dis="$(printf '%s\n' "$@")"
    create_skill "$name" "---
name: $name
description: pure review fixture
role: review

  schema_version: 1
  read_files: true
  search_code: true
  write_files: false
  execute_commands: false

  search_code: true
  write_files: true

# Writer review: review findings"
    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill writer-review
    [[ "$output" != *"pure-review skill"* ]]
    pure_review_skill bare-review2

    [[ "$output" == *"pure-review skill"* ]]
}

@test "c129-D4.2: the three pure-review skills carry the strip; rtfm-testing is a report author" {
    local s fm
    for s in eval-running flatline-knowledge validating-construct-manifest; do
        fm=$(awk '/^---$/{if(n++) exit; next} n' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/$s/SKILL.md" | yq -o=json '.')
        echo "$fm" | jq -e '.role == "review" and .capabilities.write_files == false
            and ((."disallowed-tools" | sort) == ["Edit","NotebookEdit","Write"])' >/dev/null || { echo "$s"; return 1; }
        run "$VALIDATOR" --skill "$s"
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    done
    # rtfm-testing writes its Phase 4 report (grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/), so it
    # keeps Write and strips the other two.
    fm=$(awk '/^---$/{if(n++) exit; next} n' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/rtfm-testing/SKILL.md" | yq -o=json '.')
    echo "$fm" | jq -e '.capabilities.write_files == true and (."disallowed-tools" | sort) == ["Edit","NotebookEdit"]
        and (."allowed-tools" | contains("Write"))' >/dev/null
    grep -q 'grimoires/loa/a2a/rtfm/report-' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/rtfm-testing/SKILL.md"
    run "$VALIDATOR" --skill rtfm-testing --strict
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "c129-D4.2: every role: review skill with write_files: false in the tree carries the strip" {
    local f fm n=0
    for f in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
        fm=$(awk '/^---$/{if(n++) exit; next} n' "$f" | yq -o=json '.' 2>/dev/null) || continue
        if echo "$fm" | jq -e '.role == "review" and .capabilities.write_files == false' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            n=$((n + 1))
            echo "$fm" | jq -e '(."disallowed-tools" // []) as $d | ["Write","Edit","NotebookEdit"] | all(. as $t | $d | index($t))' >/dev/null \
                || { echo "$f lacks the strip"; return 1; }
        fi
    done
    [ "$n" -ge 3 ]
}

+# Prints the heading of an optional table section; returns 1 when the section
+# is not optional.
+optional_table_heading() {
+  local section="$1" entry o_name o_heading
+  for entry in "${OPTIONAL_TABLES[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r o_name o_heading <<< "$entry"
+    if [[ "$o_name" == "$section" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$o_heading"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Removes an optional table block from FILE: the exact heading line, the
+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is
+# already pruned (no-op). Anything else between the heading and the start
+# marker, a missing heading or a missing end marker is an error and leaves
+# FILE untouched.
+prune_optional_table() {
+  local file="$1" section="$2" heading="$3"
+  if ! grep -q "@constraint-generated: start ${section} " "$file"; then
+    verbose "Optional section ${section} already absent from ${file}"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  local tmp="${file}.prune-tmp" rc=0
+  awk -v heading="$heading" \
+      -v start="@constraint-generated: start ${section} " \
+      -v end="@constraint-generated: end ${section} " '
+    function flush(   i) { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) print buf[i]; n = 0 }
+    state == "" && $0 == heading { state = "head"; n = 0; buf[++n] = $0; next }
+    state == "head" {
+      if (index($0, start)) { state = "skip"; n = 0; next }
+      if ($0 ~ /^\|/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) { buf[++n] = $0; next }
+      flush(); state = ""; print; next
+    }
+    state == "skip" { if (index($0, end)) state = "after"; next }
+    state == "after" { state = "done"; if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/) next }
+    { print }
+    END {
+      if (state == "head") flush()
+      if (state == "skip") exit 3
+      if (state == "" ) exit 4
+    }
+  ' "$file" > "$tmp" || rc=$?
+  if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
+    rm -f "$tmp"
+    case "$rc" in
+      3) log "ERROR: ${file}: no end marker for optional section '${section}'" ;;
+      4) log "ERROR: ${file}: optional section '${section}' has markers but no '${heading}' heading directly above its table" ;;
+      *) log "ERROR: ${file}: pruning optional section '${section}' failed (awk exit ${rc})" ;;
+    esac
+    return 1
+  fi
+  mv "$tmp" "$file"
+  verbose "Pruned empty optional section ${section} (${heading}) from ${file}"
+}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Lint Loa Structural Invariants
# =============================================================================
# Mechanically validates Loa's structural invariants. Run during /mount,
# /run preflight, /audit-sprint, or manually.
#
# Usage:
#   lint-invariants.sh              # Human-readable output
#   lint-invariants.sh --json       # Machine-readable JSON output
#   lint-invariants.sh --fix        # Auto-fix where possible
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = all pass
#   1 = warnings only
#   2 = errors found
#
# Part of Loa Harness Engineering (cycle-011, issue #297)
# Source: OpenAI architectural invariants + custom linter pattern
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Arguments
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
JSON_OUTPUT=false
AUTO_FIX=false
LINT_ROOT=""
HOOKS_WIRING_ONLY=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --json) JSON_OUTPUT=true; shift ;;
    --fix) AUTO_FIX=true; shift ;;
    --root)
      # bug-1002: scan an alternate project root (tests use synthetic trees)
      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "--root requires a value" >&2; exit 2; }
      LINT_ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hooks-wiring-only)
      # bug-1002: run only Invariant 7b (template<->live wiring parity)
      HOOKS_WIRING_ONLY=true; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      echo "Usage: lint-invariants.sh [--json] [--fix] [--root DIR] [--hooks-wiring-only]"
      echo ""
      echo "  --json               Output results as JSON"
      echo "  --fix                Auto-fix where possible"
      echo "  --root DIR           Lint DIR instead of the current project"
      echo "  --hooks-wiring-only  Run only the hook wiring-parity invariant"
      exit 0
      ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if [[ -n "$LINT_ROOT" ]]; then
  # Audit iter (bug-1002): a full lint run EXECUTES scripts from the lint
  # target (Invariant 8 runs test-safety-hooks.sh) — running it against an
  # untrusted checkout would execute attacker-controlled code. --root is
  # only safe for the read-only wiring check.
  if [[ "$HOOKS_WIRING_ONLY" != "true" ]]; then
    echo "--root requires --hooks-wiring-only (full lint executes scripts from the target tree)" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  cd "$LINT_ROOT" || { echo "cannot cd to --root $LINT_ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Counters
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PASSES=0
WARNINGS=0
ERRORS=0
RESULTS=()

report() {
  local level="$1"  # PASS, WARN, ERROR
  local name="$2"
  local message="$3"

    report "ERROR" "constraints" "constraints.json is invalid JSON"
    if [[ "$AUTO_FIX" == "true" ]]; then
      echo "  Cannot auto-fix invalid JSON — manual repair needed"
    fi
  fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Invariant 4: Constraint-generated blocks exist in CLAUDE.loa.md
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_constraint_blocks() {
  local file=".claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"

  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "CLAUDE.loa.md not found"
    return
  fi

  local block_count
  block_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$block_count" ]] && block_count=0

  if [[ "$block_count" -ge 3 ]]; then
    report "PASS" "constraint-blocks" "$block_count constraint-generated blocks found"
  elif [[ "$block_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    report "WARN" "constraint-blocks" "Only $block_count constraint-generated blocks (expected 3+)"
  else
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "No constraint-generated blocks found"
  fi

  # Check start/end pairs match
  local start_count end_count
  start_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: start' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  end_count=$(grep -c '@constraint-generated: end' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$start_count" ]] && start_count=0
  [[ -z "$end_count" ]] && end_count=0

  if [[ "$start_count" -ne "$end_count" ]]; then
    report "ERROR" "constraint-blocks" "Mismatched start/end pairs: $start_count starts, $end_count ends"
  fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
#
# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
# unless stated):
#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
#
# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
#
# Inputs (each has a test seam):
#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
#
# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
#
# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.
# Overrides and the requested profile name are control-stripped and cut.
# =============================================================================

_LOA_PL_SELF="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="${_LOA_PL_SELF%/*}"
[[ "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" == "$_LOA_PL_SELF" ]] && _LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="."
_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
_LOA_PL_JSON=""
_LOA_PL_ID=""

_loa_pl_paths() {
  local root="${LOA_PROFILE_ROOT:-}"
  if [[ -z "$root" ]]; then
    root="$(cd "$_LOA_PL_SELF_DIR/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)"
  fi
  _LOA_PL_ROOT="$root"
  local default_cfg="$root/.loa.config.yaml" status_cfg=""
  # LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE is loa-status.sh's bats-gated seam; honour it the same way.
  if [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
  fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
  return 0
}

loa_knob() {
  local path="${1:-}" fallback="${2:-}" key v
  key="${path#.}"
  if [[ ! "$key" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ ]]; then
    _loa_pl_warn "loa_knob: malformed key path '${path//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/?}'"
    printf '%s\n' "$fallback"
    return 2
  fi
  # Warm path: one stat + one jq straight from the cache file.
  _loa_pl_paths
  _loa_pl_id
  if [[ -z "$_LOA_PL_JSON" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" && -n "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" && -f "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" ]] &&
     command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    v=$(jq -r --arg id "$_LOA_PL_CUR_ID" --arg k "$key" '
          if .schema_version == 1 and .id == $id then
            (if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
               | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
             else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end)
          else "__LOA_PL_STALE__" end' "$_LOA_PL_CACHE" 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_STALE__"
    if [[ "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
      _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
      return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" && "$v" != "__LOA_PL_STALE__" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$v"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  if ! _loa_pl_load; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  v=$(printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r --arg k "$key" '
        if (.knobs | has($k)) then .knobs[$k].value
          | (if type == "string" then . elif type == "object" or type == "array" then tojson else tostring end)
        else "__LOA_PL_MISS__" end' 2>/dev/null) || v="__LOA_PL_MISS__"
  if [[ -z "$v" || "$v" == "__LOA_PL_MISS__" ]]; then
    _loa_pl_live "$key" "$fallback"
    return 0
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
  return 0
}

loa_profile() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile // "standard"' 2>/dev/null || echo standard
  else
    echo standard
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_source() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.profile_source // "default"' 2>/dev/null || echo default
  else
    echo default
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_profile_overrides() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s' "$_LOA_PL_JSON" | jq -r '.overrides[]?' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  return 0
}

loa_effective_json() {
  if _loa_pl_load; then
    printf '%s\n' "$_LOA_PL_JSON"
  else
    echo '{}'
  fi
  return 0
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
  export LC_ALL=C
  case "${1:-}" in
    profile)   loa_profile ;;
    source)    loa_profile_source ;;
    knob)      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "usage: profile-lib.sh knob <yq-path> [fallback]" >&2; exit 2; }
               loa_knob "$2" "${3:-}"; exit $? ;;
    overrides) loa_profile_overrides ;;
    json)      loa_effective_json ;;
    *)         sed -n '3,/^# =====/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
fi
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml — `loa.profile` defaults (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §3.5;
# DEC-0143, DEC-0152).
#
# One knob, `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` in .loa.config.yaml, sets the
# defaults of the optional surfaces below as a set. Resolution, per key
# (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh `loa_knob`):
#   1. the key set explicitly in .loa.config.yaml wins;
#   2. else the selected profile's value (unset or unknown profile → standard);
#   3. else the caller's fallback — never reached for a key listed here,
#      because every profile defines every key (tests/unit/profile-lib.bats).
#
# `standard` is the post-cycle-129 example default of each key, written out
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json records how each value was
# captured). The two guardrail keys read false here because cycle-129 changed
# their example default (D-4.4, DEC-0161): a migration item, not a profile effect.
#
# No floor key may appear here. The floor config keys are listed once, in
# .claude/data/floor.yaml `floor_keys`; tests/unit/profile-floor.bats fails if a
# profile names one, and profile-lib.sh ignores such a key with a WARN.
# `interview.pacing` is not a profile key: `rounds` is already the default and
# the key would not discriminate between profiles.
schema_version: 1

profiles:
  lean:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: false
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: false
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: false
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  standard:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: false
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: false
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: false
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: false
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: false
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: false
  full:
    known_failures.surface_at_session_start: true
    decisions.surface_at_session_start: true
    karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning: true
    karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria: true
    guardrails.input.enabled: true
    guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true
    invisible_retrospective.enabled: true
    structured_handoff.enabled: true
    soul_identity_doc.enabled: true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

import sys

anchor = "## Agent-Network Primitives"

PY
